note: Source for scripts/eif_generate_vendor_docs_guidance.py. Edit here, regenerate; do not hand-edit generated/.

use_when.trigger: A question about a library, framework, SDK, API or CLI tool's actual surface: a signature, option, configuration key or migration step.
use_when.rationale: Training data has a cutoff; a fast-moving library's API does not.

use_when.trigger: Behavior that differs between versions of a dependency the project actually pins.
use_when.rationale: Recalled behavior is frequently the behavior of a different version than the one installed.

use_when.trigger: An answer is about to be given from recall and it would be expensive to be wrong.
use_when.rationale: Confidence in recall is not evidence about the current version.

do_not_use_when.trigger: Debugging or refactoring the project's own logic.
do_not_use_when.rationale: No vendor documents this project's code; the source files do.

do_not_use_when.trigger: General programming concepts with no vendor surface.
do_not_use_when.rationale: Spends external quota for something no provider is authoritative about.

do_not_use_when.trigger: Questions about this framework's own methodology, Knowledge Delta, packets or retrieval.
do_not_use_when.rationale: That is Tier 1/Tier 2 knowledge in this repository, not vendor documentation.

boundaries: The query text leaves the local machine. Do not put private repository names, customer names, credentials or proprietary code into a vendor-docs query.
A quota-bearing provider needs an explicit cost cap in .eif/config.yaml before it is enabled.

When the provider is unavailable or its quota is exhausted, say so explicitly and fall back to local documentation or the source itself. A silent fallback to recall is the failure mode this integration exists to prevent.
Vendor documentation is normative, not empirical. If the docs and an observed test result disagree, record the discrepancy; do not overwrite the observation.
